Estimate Profile-Specific Median LOS (Section 5.3)

Source: R/daly_rr_and_los.R
daly_fit_los_distn_by_profile.Rd

For each resistance profile \(\delta\) of each pathogen \(k\), fits parametric distributions (default: Weibull, log-normal, gamma) to the LOS of the patients with that profile, \(\{LOS_i : \delta_i = \delta\}\), selects the distribution with the lowest AIC, and takes the theoretical median of the selected distribution: $$LOS_{k\delta} = Median_{f_\delta}(LOS)$$ The same procedure applied to the fully susceptible reference profile \(\delta_S\) gives \(LOS_{k\delta_S}\), and RR_LOS = LOS_{k delta} / LOS_{k delta_S}.

Usage

daly_fit_los_distn_by_profile(
  data,
  profile_data,
  patient_id_col = "PatientInformation_id",
  facility_col = "center_name",
  organism_col = "organism_name",
  syndrome_col = "syndrome",
  date_admission_col = "date_of_admission",
  date_discharge_col = "final_outcome_date",
  final_outcome_col = "final_outcome",
  final_outcome_value = "Discharged",
  profile_id_col = patient_id_col,
  profile_col = "profile_delta",
  profile_pathogen_col = NULL,
  ref_profile = NULL,
  syndrome_name = NULL,
  organism_name = NULL,
  facility_name = NULL,
  distributions = c("weibull", "lnorm", "gamma"),
  max_los = 365,
  min_n = 10L
)

Arguments

data

Data frame used for LOS (patient, facility, organism, dates, final outcome).

profile_data

Data frame with one profile per patient (or per patient x pathogen): columns profile_id_col, profile_col, and optionally profile_pathogen_col.

patient_id_col

Character. Patient identifier in data.

facility_col

Character. Facility / centre column in data.

organism_col

Character. Organism column in data; used to assign pathogens when profile_pathogen_col is NULL.

syndrome_col

Character. Syndrome column (used only with syndrome_name).

date_admission_col

Character. Admission date column.

date_discharge_col

Character. Final outcome / discharge date column.

final_outcome_col

Character. Final outcome column.

final_outcome_value

Character. Value indicating discharge.

profile_id_col

Character. ID column in profile_data matching patient_id_col. Default patient_id_col.

profile_col

Character. Profile label column in profile_data (e.g. "RRSS"). Default "profile_delta".

profile_pathogen_col

Character or NULL. Pathogen column in profile_data, when profiles are pathogen-specific. If NULL, pathogens are taken from organism_col in data.

ref_profile

Character or NULL. Label of the fully susceptible reference profile. If NULL, the label consisting only of "S" characters (e.g. "SSSS") is used per pathogen.

syndrome_name

Character or NULL. Restrict to this syndrome.

organism_name

Character vector or NULL. Restrict to these pathogens.

facility_name

Character or NULL. Restrict to this facility.

distributions

Character vector of candidate distributions. Default c("weibull", "lnorm", "gamma").

max_los

Numeric. Maximum LOS in days. Default 365.

min_n

Integer. Minimum LOS observations required to fit a profile. Default 10L.

Value

Data frame with one row per pathogen x profile: pathogen, profile_delta, is_reference, n_patients, n_los (LOS observations), median_LOS (days), median_LOS_years, best_dist, aic, median_LOS_ref, RR_LOS, status ("fitted", "insufficient_n", "fit_failed") and syndrome_scope. Profiles that cannot be fitted are kept with NA estimates.

Details

Profiles are not derived here. Each patient's resistance profile must be supplied in profile_data (e.g. the profile_delta labels from the profile_* pipeline). Patients without a profile, or with conflicting profiles, are excluded and reported in a message.

LOS is computed by daly_compute_patient_los() (final outcome date - admission date, discharged patients only, 0 < LOS <= max_los). Theoretical medians: Weibull \(\lambda (\ln 2)^{1/k}\); log-normal \(e^{\mu}\); gamma qgamma(0.5, shape, rate).

Two options for profile-level LOS

The package offers two ways to obtain LOS for each resistance profile:

  1. Profile-specific (this function; Section 5.3). Fits the LOS of the patients who actually have each profile \(\delta\) and compares it with the fully susceptible profile \(\delta_S\). Requires patient-level profiles (e.g. from the profile_* pipeline) and enough patients per profile (min_n).

  2. Per-class with max rule. daly_fit_los_rr_distribution() fits resistant vs susceptible LOS separately for each antibiotic class, then daly_assign_rr_to_profiles() gives each profile the estimate of its dominant (highest-RR) resistant class. Needs no patient-level profiles and pools data across profiles, so it is a fallback or sensitivity analysis when profiles are sparse; its reference group is "susceptible to that class", not fully susceptible.

Note: the YLD functions (daly_calc_yld_associated(), daly_calc_yld_attributable()) currently read the LOSR_years/LOSS_years columns produced by option 2; the output of this function is not yet joined into that format.

See also

daly_fit_los_rr_distribution and daly_assign_rr_to_profiles (option 2)
